title: Audio Watermarking and Source Verification
header: Thursday 1 October 2026 - 14:00-16:00 - Area 4 - Oral 7 - Audio Watermarking and Source Verification

items.title: Countering Neural Audio Codec Distortions in Watermarking with Adaptive Restoration
items.authors: Sungho Park(Soongsil University); Thien An Nguyen(Soongsil University); Souhwan Jung(Soongsil University)
items.abstract: Neural audio codecs offer high compression efficiency but introduce structured and non-linear distortions that severely degrade audio watermarks. To address this, we propose an adaptive codec-aware restoration framework that reconstructs codec-distorted spectrograms prior to extraction. Our method employs a ConvNeXt-based U-Net to recover fine-grained spectrogram patterns and introduces a lightweight classifier to dynamically select specialized restoration models for each codec. Experimental results across various neural codecs demonstrate that our model improves bitwise accuracy from near-random levels to over 98% for RVQ-based codecs. Furthermore, by analyzing the impact of quantizer configurations on watermark survivability, we show that our method can effectively improve watermark robustness in modern codec environments.

items.title: DuraMark: Duration-Embedded Watermarking in LLM-based TTS
items.authors: Zhenwei Mou(University of Science and Technology of China); Weili Jiang(Ministry of Public Security); Liping Chen(University of Science and Technology of China); Zhen-Hua Ling(University of Science and Technology of China); Kong Aik Lee(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Kai Gao(Ministry of Public Security); Boyu Zhao(Ministry of Public Security)
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) models have achieved remarkable voice cloning capabilities, raising concerns about potential deepfake misuse. Speech watermarking mitigates this by embedding traceable information into generated speech. Mainstream watermarking methods operate at the signal level (waveform or spectrogram), rendering the watermark vulnerable to generative attacks (e.g., neural codec and vocoder). To address this, we propose DuraMark, a robust information-level watermarking framework. It utilizes syllable duration editing to achieve watermark embedding. Specifically, DuraMark integrates a duration-controllable LLM-based TTS model to edit syllable durations during synthesis, coupled with a duration extractor to extract these durations for detection. Experiments demonstrate DuraMark’s superior robustness against generative attacks, significantly outperforming signal-level baselines. Audio samples are available at https://muzw.github.io/duramark_demo/.

items.title: AudioNoisePrints: Model-free audio watermarking using spatial correlation in flow matching TTS
items.authors: Timothy Tin-Long Tse(National Research Council Canada; University of British Columbia); Jian Zhu(University of British Columbia); Aidan Pine(National Research Council Canada); Mengzhe Geng(National Research Council Canada)
items.abstract: We present AudioNoisePrints, a training-free watermarking pipeline for flow matching and diffusion TTS models, which requires minimal extra computation during inference and does not require retraining the TTS model or reducing the generation quality. We exploited the fact that there are strong correlations between the initial Gaussian noises and the generated outputs in diffusion and flow matching models, such that a simple cosine correlation between the initial noise and the generated output can be used to perform watermaking. Moreover, we train a lightweight detector on top for more aggressive augmentations. Our method outperforms AudioSeal, a strong baseline for audio watermarking under strong augmentations. We experimented on F5TTS and other TTS and vocoder models, and concluded that they all exhibit similar spatial correlation properties, suggesting our watermarking scheme can be used for more flow-matching TTS models and even vocoders in the future.

items.title: VoxWatermark: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Audio Watermark Detection under Perturbations
items.authors: Farnaz Sedaghati(University of Tehran); Yuxi Wang(Nanyang Technological University); Zicheng Weng(Nanyang Technological University); Wei Rao(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: With the rapid deployment of speech generation systems in open environments, providing verifiable source attribution and copyright accountability for audio content has become critical. A gap in current research is the lack of a unified benchmark that systematically compares different watermark injection methods under realistic distribution shifts. To address this, we build VoxWatermark by applying 10 watermarking methods (4 neural and 6 traditional) with unified injection and annotation on multilingual, multi-source corpora, and introducing no-box, black-box, and white-box perturbations to simulate real recording and transmission conditions. Based on this benchmark, we propose AudioWMD as a robust baseline detector for large-scale, multi-method, cross-distribution settings. Results show that injection-method diversity and distribution shifts affect detection stability, while validating the effectiveness and scalability of AudioWMD. Dataset and code are publicly available.

items.title: Phoneme-Aware Mamba Watermark: An Active Defense System Against Purified Speech Deepfakes
items.authors: Yanda Shao(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Mengke Zhang(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Zhixin Lin(Beijing Institute of Technology); Tianyi Yang(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications)
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Voice Conversion (VC), forged speech has reached a highly realistic level, posing serious threats to voice biometrics. Traditional passive detection methods suffer from limited generalization against unseen synthesis models. In this paper, we propose a phoneme-aware active watermarking defense built on the Mamba framework. Leveraging a Dual-column Bidirectional State Space Model, the system captures long-range dependencies and covertly embeds identity bitstrings into speech. To resist diffusion-based purification attacks such as PhonePuRe, we introduce a phoneme-guided embedding mechanism that tightly couples the watermark with speech semantics, ensuring transfer to forged speech during speaker adaptation. Experiments demonstrate effective source tracing with ultra-low latency (about 1 s) and high True Positive Rate under strong purification attacks. Source code is available at https://github.com/Silence-ai423/ phoneme-aware-mamba-watermark.

items.title: The Hidden Cost of Pairwise Verification in Synthetic Speech Source Tracing
items.authors: Anton Firc(Brno University of Technology); Zbyněk Lička(Brno University of Technology); Vojtěch Staněk(Brno University of Technology); Kamil Malinka(Brno University of Technology)
items.abstract: Open-set source tracing is increasingly framed as a verification problem, motivating the use of pairwise metric-learning objectives from biometrics. We thus compare global anchoring and pairwise verification under matched backbones and a fixed data and epoch budget on MLAAD (in-domain) and STOPA (out-of-domain). In our runs, global anchoring yields lower in-domain error (8.61% EER) than pairwise variants (12-15% EER), even with rival mining and XLS-R finetuning. Because pairwise objectives optimize similarity directly, they concentrate variance into fewer embedding directions, reducing resolution among closely related generators. To test if this drives the drop, we impose a similar bottleneck to the globally supervised baseline, yet the baseline remains competitive. Together with an embedding-space analysis (k99), these results suggest that the gap is not explained by dimensionality alone, but rather by the pairwise objective's shaping of the retained directions.
